The route label alone is insufficient to establish those grade-level conclusions. Compare current grade-specific optical and colour data, treatment information, durability evidence, methods and test conditions, then validate the properties that matter in the intended system.

Does the production route alone establish lower environmental impact?

No. A chloride or sulfate label by itself is not an environmental ranking. Environmental assessment depends on the defined system boundary and factors such as feedstock, plant configuration, energy source, emissions controls, waste or by-product management, geography and the measurement or life-cycle-assessment basis used. Compare current evidence for the relevant producer, site and methodology rather than assigning a universal environmental advantage to either route.
